institutionName: Western Norway University of Applied Sciences (HVL)

questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: I choose my destination beacuse of the nature and the subject Friluftsliv

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was okay to find the information about the course and there was some meetings before going.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: We got showned around in the introduction week by local students and got important messages.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: There were an organisation Sammen, which had different student housing you could apply for. When you are an international student in Sogndal, you have housing garanty. But you get one room with another international student, which can be a bit intens. I would recommend people to apply for a single room.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: There where a kitchen with most kitchen eqiutment.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living in on campus housing? *
questions.answer: the housing is not very social. I lived in Stedjeåsen, which was a fine place and with nice people, but in a lot of the other housing you dont talk a lot to your roommates.

Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: I applied for the course: Outdoor education which was a full semeter subject, 30 ects.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: I cant remember

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: i got the class i wanted and i think everyone of the internationals got there choosen subject.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Check the deadlines and read the eqiutments list and the course describtion

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA classes while you were on exchange *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I took the course Outdoor education and Nordic friluftsliv. The courses consisted of some teaching in classrooms and a lot outside on excursions. The course is not hard. it is more learning by doing, than reading a lot.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: The courses consisted of a lot of multible day excursions and also some lectures and classroom classes.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Outdoor education and nordic friluftsliv, which consisted of the courses on 15 ects. 
Outdoor leadership
Friluftsliv, nature and culture

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
I would reccoment theses two courses. the course is only for internationals and get to know people really well and fast beacuse of the excursions. Also you get a lot of experienced in nature you would not get on Copenhagen university.
If you like to be outside, like to move and would like a less academic subject, then pick this.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: Encounter some money for equitment, beacuse you need some good eqitment for this course. You can buy most of it in Norway for around the same price as home.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Food was more expensive and especially alcohol. But else it was pretty much the same as denmark

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer:
There is some different studentorganisations which do sports, friluftsliv (hiking, climbing) and watersports
They do a lot of fun activities you should join and a lot of fun weekendtrips.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
i would recommend joning these studentorganisations. I joined lurkalaget and went on some of there fun trips (surftrip, via ferrata, climbing) and also studentspretten
I also joined the svimingclub in the fjord, which was fun. 
Also being a member of these organisations and doing the activities, make you meet new people and get in contact with the Norwegians.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer:
I recommend to go out in nature. Go for hikes in the area, camp outside, go for roadtrips, there is such amazing nature in Norway and around Sogndal. Use the DNT huts, cheap and so many opportunities. 
I also went to Lofoten in my holiday, that was amazing.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: it was pretty easy. Danish and Norwegians culture is very simular.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the different studentorganisations and join the different activities they do. You can meet a lot of local students and also be open and start a conversation, they can be a bit reserved in the begining, but they will open up.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I loved the nature, so amazing and totally different than Denmark. The studentlife was also special. The student engage in a lot of things and planned so many cool activities.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Try a lot of new things. 
Use the nature and the opportunities it gives you
Enjoy it.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Dont be nervous it is gonna be fun. And you dont need to be experienced in friluftsliv to take the course Outdoor education, people had very different backgrounds and experience.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer:
All the cool new things i tried and the expereinces i got with my new friends. 
I meet some really nice people.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Being away from my friends and family.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
